From PLIDA B1 practice paper 1, reading

Una lettera alla rivista

Mi chiamo Teresa e ho sessantasette anni. Fino all'anno scorso non avevo neanche il computer: per me la tecnologia era una cosa per i giovani. Poi mia figlia si è trasferita in Germania per lavoro e ho capito che dovevo imparare, se volevo vedere i miei nipoti più spesso che a Natale.

Teresa ha deciso di imparare a usare la tecnologia perché…

  1. voleva leggere il giornale su internet.
  2. il corso del Comune non costava niente.
  3. voleva sentire e vedere più spesso la famiglia lontana.
  4. sua figlia le aveva regalato un tablet.

Every word in a paper can be tapped for its meaning and forms while you practise.

The exams

What the three B1 exams ask

Each certificate has six levels aligned to the CEFR, and each level is a separate exam. At B1 they test the same four skills, but they divide them differently and pass you by different rules.

CILS UNO-B1CELI 2PLIDA B1
Awarded byUniversità per Stranieri di Siena (Centro CILS)Università per Stranieri di Perugia (CVCL)Società Dante Alighieri
Listening3 parts, 30 minutes3 tasks, 33 items, 20 minutes4 parts, 20 items, about 40 minutes
Reading3 parts, 50 minutes5 tasks, 37 items, which include grammar4 parts, 18 items, 40 minutes
Language structuresA test of its own: 4 parts, 60 minutesWithin readingNo separate test
WritingA description of 100 to 120 words and an informal email of 50 to 80 words, 70 minutesA form, a short announcement and a letter of 90 to 100 words; reading and writing share 2 hoursTwo guided texts of 110 to 150 and 70 to 100 words, 60 minutes
Speaking2 tasks, 10 minutes3 tasks, 10 to 12 minutes after about 12 minutes of preparation3 parts, about 15 minutes
To pass11 of 20 in each of the five tests72 of 120 points in the written part and 22 of 40 in speaking18 of 30 in each of the four tests
If you fail part of itRetake only the failed tests within 18 monthsKeep the part you passed for one year and retake the otherKeep the tests you passed for 18 months and resit the others
Glossa's B1 papersListening 16, reading 27, language use 30 and writing 70 minutesReading 38, writing 50 and listening 10 minutesListening 22, reading 22 and writing 60 minutes

Based on the published descriptions of the Università per Stranieri di Siena, the Università per Stranieri di Perugia and the Società Dante Alighieri, checked in October 2026. Check their pages for the current format.

Citizenship and residence

Which exam the papers follow

The Società Dante Alighieri states that the Italian state recognises PLIDA B1 for citizenship applications and names A2 as the level for the EU residence permit. The other two boards run separate versions for particular groups, which Glossa's papers do not follow:

  • PLIDA B1: Glossa's papers follow the ordinary B1 exam.
  • PLIDA A2: Glossa's papers follow the ordinary A2 exam taken abroad. Candidates in Italy take PLIDA A2 inItalia, with the same four tests and pass rule but 45 minutes for writing and about 12 for speaking.
  • CILS: the version for citizenship (B1 cittadinanza) is a separate exam. Glossa's papers follow the standard UNO-B1.
  • CELI: the CVCL also runs separate CELI for adult immigrants. Glossa's papers follow the general CELI.
  • The Italian authorities that handle your application decide which certificates they accept and set the other conditions.

Honest limits

How the practice papers differ from the real exams

  • No grade and no score conversion. A paper shows the share of points in each section. It does not use the boards' conversion tables, cannot give a CELI grade from A to E, and never turns writing into a PLIDA score out of 30. PLIDA weights items by difficulty; here every item counts the same.
  • Listening and reading are shorter than the real tests, about half the items in the same task types, and the time is cut to match. At B1, writing is full length.
  • There is no speaking test. All three certificates need speaking, so passing the sections of a paper does not cover the whole exam.
  • Some task formats are adapted. At CILS B1, statements you would pick from a list are marked true or false one by one; at PLIDA B1, options shown as pictures are short sentences; at CELI 2, reading and writing are timed separately instead of as one 2-hour block.
  • Recordings can be replayed, with one voice. In CILS and PLIDA you hear each recording twice. The CELI 2 description does not say how often, but the board’s CELI 1 and CELI 3 sample papers play each one twice. Play each recording twice and then answer. In dialogues both speakers are read by one voice.
  • Words can be tapped for their meaning while you practise; the real exams allow no dictionary.

Questions

Common questions

Is Glossa an official CILS, CELI or PLIDA preparation course?
No. Glossa is not connected with the Università per Stranieri di Siena, the Università per Stranieri di Perugia or the Società Dante Alighieri. The papers follow their published exam descriptions, with original content.
Which exam do I need for Italian citizenship?
The Società Dante Alighieri states that the Italian state recognises PLIDA B1 for citizenship applications; CILS has a separate citizenship version of its B1 exam. The Italian authorities that handle your application decide which certificates they accept and set the other conditions.
CILS, CELI or PLIDA: which should I take?
That depends on what the certificate is for and where you can sit it. They differ in structure: CILS has a separate language structures test and needs a pass in every test, CELI adds the written tests together and grades from A to E, and PLIDA needs 18 of 30 in each of four tests.
What is free?
The whole Italian course from A1 to C1, the grammar reference and word practice are free. The practice papers, conversation practice, stories and the other extras are part of Premium.
I speak Spanish. Is there a course for me?
Yes. Italiano para hispanohablantes has the same CILS, CELI and PLIDA papers, with the instructions and explanations in Spanish.
